title: Cohort-based shadow heatmap promoter with staged rollback heuristics
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We observed brittle promotions when shadow-to-canary conversions relied solely on global SLO pass/fail signals. For multi-cohort populations this led to noisy handoffs and repeated rollbacks. This PR implements a cohort-aware "heatmap promoter" that aggregates shadow fidelity and latency signals at the cohort level, performs progressive promotions driven by per-cohort heat thresholds, and includes an automated staged rollback heuristic that hedges on shadow signal volatility.

Summary of changes: Implements a new promotion controller (heatmap promoter) + controller shim, introduces cohort scoring and volatility metrics, extends the telemetry schema with cohort_fidelity and cohort_variability metrics, adds a promote policy CRD with conservative defaults, and wires a staged rollback heater that soft-fails promotions when volatility exceeds a threshold. Also adds dashboard and alerting panels to the rollout observability suite and a small SDK helper for evaluating cohort heatmaps in integration tests.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-9342) - [x] Controller unit tests - [x] Integration tests using simulated cohorts (local harness) - [x] E2E smoke on staging - [x] Observability dashboards and alert rules - [x] Linear ticket linked

Design notes: The promoter computes a heatmap by bucketing requests by cohort key (cookie, account_id hash, feature flags) and computing a composite fidelity score: fidelity = weighted(accuracy_ratio, latency_tail_compliance, error_rate). A volatility moving-window estimator flags cohorts with >X% variance over the last N minutes. The promote policy exposes: min_cohort_heat (float), max_volatility (float), staged_window (minutes), and fallback_model (string). Promotions only proceed for cohorts meeting min_cohort_heat and volatility <= max_volatility. If a cohort flips volatility mid-rollout, the staged rollback heater reduces traffic to the new variant in incremental steps and replays captured shadow traffic to the prior model for verification.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy promoter to staging; run synthetic cohorts for 48h. 2) Deploy to a small prod namespace (internal beta) with default conservative promote policy (min_cohort_heat=0.8, max_volatility=0.12). 3) Gradually open to additional cohorts over 72h while monitoring cohort_fidelity and cohort_variability dashboards. 4) If any cohort's volatility tripped, automatic staged rollback engages and notifies on-call. Manual override allowed via console.

Risk & mitigation: Risk: miscalibrated heat thresholds could block promotions. Mitigation: initial conservative defaults + rollout only to internal cohorts. Risk: added telemetry cardinality. Mitigation: cohort key sampling and TTL compaction by default.

Backward compatibility: promote policy fields are additive. No breaking API changes. SDK helper is optional for callers.

Testing: unit tests for promoter logic, integration tests using the eval-harness with deterministic cohort traces, and a canary on staging with replayed traffic.

Notes: This PR purposefully keeps promote policy ergonomic; followups will expose auto-calibration and richer signal fusion (model-quality + cost).
